extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and historians of mathematics; readers of the Notices of the AMS
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for assessing mathematical contributions, priority claims, and historiography of the Italian school of algebraic geometry (Castelnuovo, Enriques, Severi, Segre). Covers what to include in surveys, how to weigh contributions, and norms about rigor versus intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical perspective and hierarchy of ideas/names
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It lacks perspective so that a reader who doesn’t know much will not be able to understand the hierarchy of ideas and names.’ (Severi’s criticism of Segre’s draft.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing a historical survey or lecture, organize material so a non-expert can see the relative importance and chronological/ conceptual hierarchy of people and ideas; make clear which results are foundational versus later refinements. (Example: Segre’s published paper increased mentions of Noether after Severi’s comment.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overrating or underrating contributions; give balanced comparative evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Severi points out that some figures (e.g., C. Segre, Castelnuovo, Enriques) have been either overrated or underrated in Segre’s draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contributions comparatively and with evidence; beware of personal affection or antipathy biasing evaluations. Weigh words carefully (Severi: 'You need to weigh your words!'). Explicitly justify claims of relative importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge foundational prior work and intellectual dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Severi emphasizes that the Castelnuovo–Enriques classification was built on prior notions (geometric and arithmetic genus, Zeuthen-C. Segre invariant, Brill-Noether, Picard on surfaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In historical or evaluative accounts, list and credit the essential antecedent results and concepts that made later breakthroughs possible; avoid implying isolated genius where major groundwork existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious assigning priority where research was collaborative or suggested
rubrics_metrics.description: Castelnuovo: 'how much caution is needed when you assign scientific priorities in periods in which the research was often done in collaboration, or was suggested by elders to their more youthful colleagues.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing priority, consider unpublished letters, shared ideas, collaboration patterns, and mentoring; avoid 'overly clean divisions' and acknowledge joint or sequential contributions rather than rigid first-author claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insist on mathematical precision and logical rigor in proofs and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix: the Franco-American school criticized the Italian school for imprecise definitions and lack of logical rigor; some Italian proofs were later shown flawed and required rigorous replacements (e.g., Enriques–Severi issues, Grothendieck’s later work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mathematical work by whether definitions are precise and proofs meet community standards of rigor; note when results rest on proofs later found defective and indicate how/when rigorous proofs were obtained (e.g., transcendental proofs by Poincaré, algebraic rigor by Grothendieck, Néron refinements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the role and value of geometric intuition alongside formal methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Castelnuovo defends geometric intuition as 'the only means that so far has allowed us to find the way' and laments the 'algebraizing' trend; he warns against abandoning intuition even while acknowledging new trends toward formal rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In assessing mathematical practice, balance appreciation for intuition-driven discovery with the need for later formalization; characterize a school’s style (intuitive vs formal) and its consequences for discovery and eventual acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure significance by introduction of new ideas that solve entrenched problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Severi claims he 'developed new ideas that untied the Gordian knots' and lists specific advances (characterization of irregular surfaces, Theorem of the Base, contributions to enumerative geometry) as measures of importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a contribution provided conceptual clarifications, new viewpoints, or resolved longstanding obstacles when judging its significance, not merely technical computations or isolated lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider creation of a school (training successors) as a metric of influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Severi asserts he is 'the only one among living Italian algebraic geometers who has created a school.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track influence via students, followers, and sustained research programs; creating a 'school' (distinct methods and many successors) counts as a major sign of scientific impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct attribution and documentary awareness for major theorems (e.g., Theorem of the Base, Picard integrals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the Theorem of the Base (Néron–Severi theorem), Picard integrals, and the historical evolution of proofs (Enriques’ flawed argument, Severi’s work, Poincaré’s transcendental proof, Grothendieck's later rigorous proof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recounting the history of a theorem, record who stated and proved which parts, note the correctness or flaws of original proofs, and point to later rigorous resolutions; avoid attributing a result without clarifying the status of its proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include major results and technical milestones in surveys of a field
rubrics_metrics.description: The article emphasizes mentioning key notions and theorems (geometric/arithmetic genus, Zeuthen–Segre invariant, Brill–Noether theorem, Picard, Theorem of the Base) when treating the history of surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A historical or pedagogical survey should list and briefly explain the field’s technical milestones so readers can see conceptual development; omission of central results risks misleading readers about the field’s structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate national schools within international methodological trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Castelnuovo contrasts the Italian school’s intuition-driven style with the Franco-American school’s emphasis on formal rigor; the Appendix recounts international debates and eventual dominance of different standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a school’s methods and achievements in the context of contemporaneous international developments and debates, acknowledging both strengths and criticisms and how standards shifted over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support evaluative claims with citations, frequencies, and documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The text notes Segre’s revised paper mentions certain figures more often (counts given) after Severi’s critique, showing how evidence/citation patterns can document revision and influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back assertions about importance or neglect with documentary evidence (citations, publication counts, letters); quantitative indicators and primary-source letters can strengthen historical judgments and demonstrate response to criticism.
